title: Bhakti yoga: the nine forms of devotion; the Alvars and Nayanars; Mirabai, Tulsidas, Surdas; kirtan as method (2 of 7)
hook: nine ways to love God, and a famous name standing beside each one
tomorrow: Bhakti yoga: the nine forms of devotion; the Alvars and Nayanars; Mirabai, Tulsidas, Surdas; kirtan as method (3 of 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday: bhakti yoga, and the line love as the road. A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water. And Prahlada in his father's lap, listing nine ways to love. Today, all nine. Day two hundred sixty-eight.
screen: `A LEAF, A FLOWER, A FRUIT, WATER.`

segments.voice: People love differently. Some people say it. Some people show it with food. Some people just show up, every time, and never say a word. Some people love by listening, really listening. If you've ever been in a family, you know this: the love was all there, it just came in different shapes. Prahlada's list is the bhakti tradition noticing the same thing about loving God. It's not one feeling. It's nine doors into the same room. Tradition even gives each door a famous person who walked through it.
screen: `PEOPLE LOVE DIFFERENTLY.` → `SAY IT, SHOW IT, SHOW UP.` → `NINE DOORS, ONE ROOM.`

segments.voice: Here they are, in the order Prahlada gives them in the Bhagavata Purana. One: shravana, hearing. Listening to the stories of God. Tradition's example is King Parikshit, who heard the entire Bhagavata in his last seven days. Two: kirtana, singing. Praising aloud: the sage Shuka, who told Parikshit those stories. Three: smarana, remembering. Keeping God in mind: Prahlada himself. Four: pada-sevana, serving the feet. Humble, close service: the goddess Lakshmi, at Vishnu's feet. Five: archana, worship with offerings, lamp and flower and water: King Prithu. Six: vandana, bowing and praising: Akrura, who bowed to the ground when he met Krishna. Seven: dasya, being a servant: Hanuman, who wanted nothing but to serve Rama. Eight: sakhya, friendship: Arjuna, whose chariot Krishna drove into battle, as a friend. Nine: atma-nivedana, giving your whole self: King Bali, who gave everything he had, even his own head to be stepped on. Notice how the list moves. It starts with the ear, then the voice, then the mind. Then the hands, then the whole body bowing. Then relationships, servant, then friend. And it ends with a person handing over themselves. It's a ladder, and it's also a menu. Most people, teachers say, find one or two doors that fit them and live there for years. A grandmother who can't sit through a sermon but sings every evening. A quiet man who never sings but sweeps the temple steps. Same room.
screen: `THE EAR, THE VOICE, THE MIND.` · `THE HANDS AND THE BOWED HEAD.` · `SERVANT, THEN FRIEND.` · `GIVING YOUR WHOLE SELF.` · then, large: `LOVE AS THE ROAD.`

segments.voice: Sit, and walk slowly past the nine doors. Hearing. Singing. Remembering. Serving. Offering. Bowing. Serving as a servant. Friendship. Giving yourself. Which one pulls at you? Don't choose the one you think is best. Choose the one that feels like home. Stay with it. If you pray, you can walk through that door now, quietly. If you don't, just notice which shape your love usually takes, with anyone. The bell holds the time.
Bhakti yoga. The nine forms of devotion, navadha bhakti: hearing, singing, remembering, serving, worship, bowing, servanthood, friendship and giving yourself.
Your line: love as the road. Today, try your door once, deliberately. Listen to one story, sing one line, or serve one person, quietly and fully. Day two hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Hindu devotional teachers often present the nine forms of bhakti from the Bhagavata Purana as a range of practices, from listening to sacred stories and singing to service and complete self-offering, and devotees tend to settle into the forms that suit them.

fork.setup: a grandmother can't follow a long sermon, but sings to Krishna every evening. by the nine forms, is she practicing bhakti?
options: no: she has to learn the philosophy first.
yes: kirtana, singing, is one of the nine doors.
only if she also does all eight others.
fork.reveal: singing, kirtana, is the second of the nine. each door opens into the same room.

original.note: Sanskrit: navadhā bhakti, devotion in nine forms (nava, nine), as listed in the Bhagavata Purana 7.5.23–24.

trapdoor: what you thought: devotion is a single feeling.
what it means: bhakti has nine recognized forms, from hearing to giving your whole self.

what a scholar hears: the list is Bhagavata Purana 7.5.23–24; the pairing of each form with an exemplar (Parikshit, Shuka, Prahlada, Lakshmi, Prithu, Akrura, Hanuman, Arjuna, Bali) comes from a later devotional verse cited by Gaudiya and other Vaishnava teachers.
